findings.title: Session cookie not marked Secure in production
findings.notes: ProductionConfig sets SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = False, so the browser also sends the Flask session cookie over plain HTTP where it can be intercepted (session hijacking on a downgraded or mixed-content request). Impact is limited by HTTPS deployment and SameSite=Lax. No built-in SAST rule covers Flask config attributes. Fix: set it to True in production.

negatives.description: Every per-document route loads through owned_document_or_404, which filters by owner and answers 404; not an IDOR.
send_from_directory with the fixed upload directory and a server-generated stored name; not path traversal.
SQLAlchemy ORM query with bound parameters; not SQL injection.
?next= passes through _safe_next, which only allows same-site relative paths; not an open redirect.
Share tokens come from the secrets module (256 bits) and expire; not predictable tokens.
Intentionally public download, authorized by an unguessable, expiring share token rather than a login; not missing authentication.
SECRET_KEY is read from the environment with no fallback; not a hard-coded secret.
CSRF is disabled only in TestingConfig (APP_ENV=testing); production uses CSRFProtect.
User-supplied notes rendered through Jinja2 autoescaping (no |safe); not XSS.
Uploads are stored under a random server-side name, so the client filename never reaches the filesystem path.
